title: Germany – Technical inspection and testing services – Rahmenvertrag Prüfung elektrischer Anlagen und Betriebsmittel nach DGUV Vorschrift 3
description: Die Ausführung von Prüfungen von elektrischen Anlagen und Betriebsmitteln nach DGUV Vorschrift 3 werden für die Liegenschaften am Flughafen Köln/Bonn ausgeschrieben. Die Leistungen beinhalten ebenfalls die Erstellung und Überarbeitung von Gefährdungsbeurteilungen nach Betriebssicherheitsverordnung (BetrSichV) und TRBS 1111. Gemäß Betriebssicherheitsverordnung (BetrSichV) sowie Sozialgesetzbuch ist der Betreiber von ortsveränderlichen und ortsfesten Elektrogeräten, Anlagen und Betriebsmitteln zur Durchführung von wiederkehrenden Prüfungen gemäß Unfallverhütungsvorschrift DGUV V3 der Berufsgenossenschaften durchzuführen und zu dokumentieren. Mit der Wiederholungsprüfung sollen eventuelle Abnutzungen oder Beschädigungen rechtzeitig erkannt werden, sofern sie sicherheitstechnisch relevant sind. Ferner soll sie den sicherheitstechnisch einwandfreien Zustand der Anlage und des Betriebsmittels belegen, damit es weiterhin benutzt werden kann. Mit der Erstinbetriebnahmeprüfung von elektrischen Betriebsmitteln soll sichergestellt werden, dass diese den Anforderungen der elektrotechnischen Regeln und den Verordnungen zum Geräte- und Produktsicherheitsgesetz (EU-Konformität) entsprechen und somit als sichere Arbeitsmittel in Betrieb gehen. Die vorgenannten Prüfungen sind Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung. Die Prüfungen sind durch Elektrofachkräfte durchzuführen. Messungen sind mit geeigneten und kalibrierten Prüfmitteln gemäß DIN EN/IEC 61557 (VDE 0413-x) durchzuführen.

title: EL-26-11 Rammeavtale Taxitjenester
description: Bakgrunn og formål Elverum kommune skal gjennomføre en ny anskaffelse av taxitjenester. Anskaffelsen skal dekke kommunens behov for drosjetransport som ikke omfattes av andre transportavtaler (eks. skoleskyss, transport til aktiviteter og ulike typer turkjøring). Kommunen har løpende behov for persontransport innen blant annet skole, helse- og mestringstjenester (HMO) og barnevern, men alle sektorer og enheter kan ha behov for tjenesten. Rammeavtalen vil kunne omfatte både planlagte og akutte transportoppdrag. Anskaffelsen skal bidra til en helhetlig, forutsigbar og effektiv løsning for kommunens transportbehov. Formålet med anskaffelsen er å inngå en rammeavtale for taxitjenester som sikrer trygg, fleksibel og kostnadseffektiv persontransport, med tilstrekkelig kapasitet, høy leveringssikkerhet og god tilgjengelighet tilpasset kommunens behov. Omfang Estimert verdi er kun et estimat. Kommunens behov vil variere fra år til år, og endringer i organisering, budsjett og rutiner kan påvirke totalvolumene. Dette er en rammeavtale, og medfører ingen kjøpeplikt for kommunen.

title: A borehole geophysical logging system for hydrogeological investigations in fractured crystalline bedrock
description: A borehole geophysical logging system for hydrogeological investigations in fractured crystalline bedrock Procurement of a borehole geophysical logging system for hydrogeological investigations in fractured crystalline bedrock. The system shall include a wireline winch, a surface data acquisition unit, a three-arm caliper, a spinner flowmeter, a heat-pulse flowmeter, compatible accessories, and the necessary software. The equipment shall be suitable for measurements in deep, inclined, water-filled boreholes with nominal diameters of 56 mm and 76 mm, at operational depths of up to 1000 m measured along the borehole axis. All supplied components shall be mutually compatible and suitable for field operation. See the minimum requirements in the section Criteria for the object of procurement. Hankinnan kohteena on porareikien geofysikaalinen mittausjärjestelmä hydrogeologisiin tutkimuksiin rikkonaisessa kiteisessä kallioperässä. Järjestelmän tulee sisältää vaijerivinssi, pinnalla käytettävä tiedonkeruuyksikkö, kolmihaarainen kaliiperimittari, spinner-virtausmittari, lämpöpulssivirtausmittari, yhteensopivat lisävarusteet sekä tarvittavat ohjelmistot. Laitteiston tulee soveltua mittauksiin syvissä, kaltevissa ja vedellä täyttyneissä tutkimusrei’issä, joiden nimellishalkaisijat ovat 56 mm ja 76 mm. Laitteiston tulee mahdollistaa mittaukset 1000 metrin syvyyteen asti porareiän akselia pitkin mitattuna. Kaikkien toimitettavien komponenttien tulee olla keskenään yhteensopivia ja soveltua kenttäkäyttöön. Katso vähimmäisvaatimukset kohdasta hankinnan kohteen kriteerit.,

title: Germany – Administration, defence and social security services – [J4-25V-012] Neukonzeptionierung des "Handbuch der Ergonomie"
description: Das Handbuch der Ergonomie (HdE) ist eine umfangreiche Sammlung ergonomischen Fachwissens. Es dient dem Auftraggeber (AG) als zentrale mitgeltende Unterlage im Beschaffungsprozess und stellt eine unverzichtbare Säule für die Beantwortung ergonomischer Fragestellungen dar, mit dem Ziel, eine hohe Qualität in der Beschaffung und Entwicklung von Produkten zu gewährleisten. Gleichzeitig enthält es Daten und Angaben für Auftragnehmer (AN), wie Geräte/ Produkte ergonomisch konstruiert und ausgelegt werden. Ziel der im Rahmen des Vertrags zu erbringenden und im Folgenden näher beschriebenen Leistungen ist es, für die sowohl strukturelle als auch inhaltliche Gesamtüberarbeitung des HdE ein detailliertes Konzept zu erarbeiten, welches als Grundlage für die spätere Umsetzung dient: • Das Konzept soll basierend auf Bedarfsanalysen verschiedener Nutzergruppen neu ausgerichtet werden. Der Fokus soll hier auf einer Nutzbarkeit für die Bundeswehr und deren Bedürfnisse liegen. (Arbeitspaket 2) • Das HdE muss fachlich analysiert sowie auf seine Aktualität hin geprüft werden. (Arbeitspaket 3) • Erstellung von drei Konzepten, die das HdE zeitgemäß und übersichtlich aufbereiteten. Ein Konzeptvorschlag soll detailliert ausgearbeitet werden. (Arbeitspaket 4) • Neben der Erarbeitung des Konzeptes sollen alle notwendigen Vorarbeiten für die Gesamtüberarbeitung vorgenommen sowie geeignete Autoren für die Überarbeitung identifiziert werden. (Arbeitspaket 5)

title: APN_Construction of Training Quarters Buildings 2 and 3, CFB Borden ON
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE Construction of Training Quarters Buildings 2 and 3 CFB Borden, Ontario (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Borden, Ontario. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following 2-Step (Step 1: Request for Expression of Interest, Step 2: Tender Phase) solicitation will proceed as noted below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN Number: 88280 Approximate Estimate: $168 million for both buildings Anticipated Posting Step 1: January 2027 Anticipated Posting Step 2: February 2027 Description: The project comprises the construction of two new five-storey training quarters buildings at CFB Borden, Ontario. The buildings will use a site-adapted design based on the existing Training Quarters Building S-166. The anticipated work includes building construction, mechanical and electrical systems, associated site development and connections to site services. The design will incorporate site-specific requirements and lessons learned from the existing building.  3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a tenderer or proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security screening requirement for each construction contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors or consultants early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors or consultants that intend to submit a tender or a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential tenderers or proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors or consultants are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors or consultants to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor or consultant: Have submitted a response to the Step 1: RFEOI, have submitted a Sponsorship application prior to the date of publication of the Step 2: Tender Phase, meet all material requirements of the sponsorship application package by the closing date of the Step 2: Tender Phase, and Have submitted a tender to the Step 2: Tender Phase. DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors or Consultants that do not submit a tender will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the tenderer or proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Victor Shekofteh Contract Coordinator Defence Construction Canada 249-535-4651 victor.shekofteh@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the tenderer or proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the tenderer or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: NPP - Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector
description: Trade Agreement: CFTA, Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Colombia Free Trade agreement, Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement. Tendering Procedures: to all pre-qualified suppliers under the Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI under Crystallography Equipment. Competitive Procurement Strategy: Lowest cost Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: No Nature of Requirements: Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector THIS REQUEST IS RESERVED FOR HOLDERS OF SUPPLY ARRANGEMENT # E60PV-19EQUI ONLY, FOR THE PURCHASE OF LABORATORY AND SCIENTIFIC EQUIPMENT, PARTS AND ACCESSORIES, SERVICES AND SUPPLIES. Only Suppliers currently pre-qualified on Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI have been invited to bid. As a requirement of the Supply Arrangement, this notice is published on Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) for a period of 40 calendar days. The closing date published on this notice identifies how long the notice will be published. For the closing date of any solicitation under the supply arrangement, invited suppliers should refer to the solicitation documents. Suppliers that do not have a Supply Arrangement for the supply of Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies with Public Works and Government Services Canada, cannot submit a bid. Any bids received from suppliers not pre-qualified on the Supply Arrangement will not be evaluated. Suppliers may qualify under Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI for Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies, at any time. Interested suppliers should download solicitation document E60PV-19EQUI/D from CanadaBuys (SAP Ariba) and submit a response as per the requirements of the Request for Supply Arrangement. Item : Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector Quantity: 1 The mandatory technical criteria are: # MANDATORY TECHNICAL CRITERIA M1 Must be capable of being installed on a TESCAN Mira3 XMH model scanning electron microscope M2 Must come equipped with a CMOS sensor, a phosphor screen, and fibre-optic coupling M3 Must be capable of collecting EBSD patterns with image sizes up to 1244x1024 M4 Must have pattern acquisition speeds of up to 5700 patterns per second at 156x128 resolution M5 Must allow analyses at beam currents as low as 400 pA and accelerating voltages as low as 5kV M6 Must be capable of angular resolution up to 0.05 degrees M7 Must have motorized screen elevation control and insertion/retraction control M8 Must come equipped with a 5 diode forescatter diode (FSD) array for orientation contrast, topographic contrast, and atomic number contrast imaging M9 Must come with a Windows PC workstation installed with software for data acquisition and processing. M10 Must be capable of simultaneous EDS/EBSD mapping with an X-Max 80 model EDS detector, permitting refined phase identification using sample chemistry. Note: The X-Max 80 is the exact model of EDS detector currently installed in the laboratory. We rely on a function where simultaneously collected EDS data is used to aid in the correct identification of crystallographically similar phases during automated EBSD analyses, and therefore any new EBSD detector must be compatible with our X-Max 80.

description: This Contract covers the preparation of investment-ready documentation for 50 pre-selected local public buildings in the municipalities of Berat, Shkodër, Korçë and Përmet, including offices, kindergartens, libraries, and social and cultural centres. The Assignment includes the preparation of energy audits, detailed technical designs, building permit documentation, Bills of Quantities, Environmental and Social Management Plans, and PRAG-compliant tender documentation. All 50 buildings will be assessed and prioritised in accordance with DCM No. 468/2024 . Based on this prioritisation, buildings with a total gross floor area of at least 22,000 m² will be selected for the implementation of energy-efficiency measures under a subsequent Works Contract. The Contract also includes the supervision of the civil works implemented in the selected buildings. The Service Contract is structured in two phases, comprising a total of 60 months of service provision, with a 12-month interim period between the two phases. Phase 1, lasting 24 months, covers the energy audit, preparation of the detailed technical design and preparation of the tender dossier for the Works Contract. This phase will be followed by a 12-month interim period, during which the procurement procedure for the Works Contract is expected to take place and no services will be required under the Service Contract. Phase 2, lasting 36 months, will cover the supervision and monitoring of the Works, commencing upon the start of the Works Contract.

title: Table-Top Free Space Measuring System - USDA-ARS Auburn AL
description: This is a Sources Sought notice Only. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. This Sources Sought is issued for information and planning purposes only as part of USDA ARS market research and does not itself constitute an RFQ. This requirement is covered under NAICS code 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified sources; Small Businesses; HUBZone small business; service-disabled, veteran-owned small business; 8(a) small business; veteran-owned small business; woman-owned small business; or small disadvantaged businesses; Responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. The USDA-ARS National Soil Dynamics laboratory (NSDL) is in need of a specialized microwave instrument which enables the user to measure reflection and transmission data while not touching nor destroying (NDE) the sample. The following are the specification required for this instrument. 1. Small table-top frame for transmission and reflection measurements. 2. The frame with two probes at the proper alignment and distance for optimal measurements and has a versatile sample holder to allow for multiple specimen types and sizes. 3. The frame with two probes for a frequency range of at least 2.5 GHz to 20 GHz. 4. At least one pair of SMA cables designed for use up to at least 25 GHz. 5. Two probes should be able to be connected to a VNA. 6. Software for VNA that calculates the S-parameters. 7. Free Space Measurement Methods to characterize materials. 8. Enables the user to measure reflection and transmission of electromagnet waves data while not touching nor destroying (NDE) the sample The Government does not intend to make an award based on responses to this inquiry. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Capability Statement All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. title: Office of Hazardous Materials Safety Research Initiative � FY2026 BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA)
description: The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), Office of Hazardous Materials Safety (OHMS), is soliciting white papers and full proposals under Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) PHMSA-26HM-BAA pursuant to FAR 35.016. The objective of this announcement is to award competitive research contracts that advance scientific, technical, engineering, and policy solutions to prevent incidents and enhance safety during the transportation of hazardous materials across all modes. Offerors are invited to submit innovative research proposals addressing one or more of the following core topic areas: 26HM-ESS (Efficient Safety Standards): Research to modernize safety standards and testing, streamline certification, leverage safety data, and evaluate risk landscapes to reduce regulatory burden while maintaining safety. 26HM-SST (Safe Energy Storage Technologies): Research assessing transportation risks of energy storage systems, battery chemistries, thermal runaway detection and mitigation, and critical mineral recovery. 26HM-IPG (Innovative Packaging): Development and evaluation of advanced packaging materials, containment designs, integrity monitoring, and predictive failure simulations. 26HM-RER (Risk Reduction for Emergency Response): Innovations, technologies, data analysis, and materials to enhance emergency responder safety, communication, and preparedness. 26HM-RTS (Hazardous Materials Rail Transportation Safety): Research advancing scientific understanding of rail tank car performance under derailment conditions, crashworthiness materials, thermal shielding, and predictive risk modeling. A two-phase selection process (Phase I: White Paper; Phase II: Invited Full Proposal) will be used. Awards will be procurement contracts (Firm-Fixed-Price or Cost-Reimbursement) up to $2,000,000 with a total performance period of up to 36 months. Full eligibility, formatting, and submission instructions are detailed in the solicitation document attached to this notice.

description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS / SOLICITATION FOR COMMERCIAL SERVICES Solicitation Number: 30326PR270000001 Project Title: USCG Station Cortez 2nd Deck Carpet Removal and Luxury Vinyl Plank (LVP) Flooring Installation Issuing Agency: United States Coast Guard (USCG) � Base Miami Beach (P&C) Notice Type: Combined Synopsis / Solicitation Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside Applicable NAICS Code: 238330 � Flooring Contractors Small Business Size Standard: $19.0 Million Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Acquisition Authority: FAR Subpart 12.6 (Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Items), FAR Part 13 (Simplified Acquisition Procedures), and FAR Part 15 1. General Notice & Acquisition Overview This document constitutes a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services and minor facility improvements prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Sole Solicitation: This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; no separate written solicitation will be issued. Set-Aside: The solicitation is advertised as a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. Offers received from entities other than small business concerns will not be considered. Basis of Award: Award will be made using simplified acquisition procedures to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to all solicitation requirements and represents the Best Value to the Government, considering technical approach, past performance, and price. Performance Requirement: The contractor shall provide all management, tools, equipment, materials, labor, and supervision required to remove existing carpet and install new Luxury Vinyl Plank (LVP) flooring and vinyl base molding across approximately 2,887 sq. ft. on the 2nd Deck of the Multipurpose Building at USCG Station Cortez. 2. Key Procurement Schedule & Contacts Organized Site Visit December 08, 2026 @ 9:00 AM EST Location: USCG Station Cortez, Bradenton, FL. Coordination POC: MKC Adam Muniz, Station EPO Email: Adam.L.Muniz@uscg.mil (Prior coordination required for gate access and escort). Proposal Submission Deadline December 22, 2026 @ 1:00 PM EST Electronic submission via email to the Contracting Officer. Period of Performance Within 45 calendar days post-award Work to commence no later than 15 calendar days post-award and reach final inspection within 45 calendar days. Authorized Work Hours Mon � Fri, 0800 � 1600 (8:00 AM � 4:00 PM EST) Work outside these hours requires prior written authorization from the Station EPO. No weekends or federal holidays authorized. Points of Contact Contracting Officer / Contract Specialist (Contractual & Submission Inquiries): Ulric Waldron, Contracting Officer / Specialist Email: Ulric.Waldron@uscg.mil Mailing / Delivery Address: Commanding Officer USCG Base Miami Beach (P&C) Attn: Ulric Waldron 16001 SW 117th Avenue Miami, FL 33177 Technical Point of Contact / Station EPO (Site Visit & Technical Inquiries): MKC Adam Muniz, Engineering Petty Officer (EPO) USCG Station Cortez Email: Adam.L.Muniz@uscg.mil 3. Place of Performance Facility: USCG Station Cortez Building: Multipurpose Building (2nd Deck) Physical Address: 4530 124th St. Ct. W. Bradenton, FL 34209 4. Proposal Submission Instructions 4.1 Submission Methods & Protocols Electronic Submission (Preferred): Quotes must be submitted electronically via email to Ulric.Waldron@uscg.mil and carbon-copy (CC) Adam.L.Muniz@uscg.mil. Telephone or verbal quotes will not be accepted. Mail / Hand Delivery: Hand-delivered or courier submissions must arrive at USCG Base Miami Beach (P&C), Attn: Ulric Waldron, 16001 SW 117th Avenue, Miami, FL 33177 prior to 1:00 PM EST on December 22, 2026. Amendments: Formal amendments and notices of changes will be published via SAM.gov. Offerors must acknowledge all amendments in their quotation. 4.2 Mandatory Email Subject Formatting Inquiries and proposals without the exact subject line formats may experience severe processing and response delays: Proposal Submission Subject Format: [PROPOSAL SUBMISSION] [30326PR270000001] - [Station Cortez 2nd Deck Carpet Replacement] ([Company Name]) Question / Clarification Subject Format: [QUESTION SUBMISSION] [30326PR270000001] - [Station Cortez 2nd Deck Carpet Replacement] ([Company Name]) (Note: Replace [Company Name] with your organization's legal name inside the parentheses). 4.3 Vendor Administrative Requirements Entity Identification: Offerors must provide their legal business name, Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN/EIN), CAGE code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Active SAM Registration: Offerors must maintain an ACTIVE registration in SAM.gov at the time of proposal submission, prior to award, and throughout performance. NAICS Registration: Offerors should have NAICS code 238330 (Flooring Contractors) or related construction/renovation NAICS listed on their SAM profile. 4.4 Proposal Package Content Requirements To be deemed responsive, offerors must submit: Price Quote: A completed firm-fixed-price schedule breaking down labor, materials (LVP, adhesive, baseboards), subfloor preparation/grinding, and debris disposal. Technical Approach: Narrative demonstrating understanding of the Scope of Work (SOW), dust containment plan, installation methodology per manufacturer specifications, and estimated project schedule. Key Personnel Information: Identification of the Project Manager (PM) and designated alternate(s) including contact details and qualifications. Safety Plan: Written safety plan in compliance with FAR 52.236-13 and OSHA standards (29 CFR 1926). Past Performance References: At least two (2) references for recent, similar flooring/commercial renovation projects executed within the last three (3) years. 5. Areas covered include: Crew berthing spaces Administrative offices Communication Watchstander room Exclusions: This scope does not include upgrades to unrelated building systems, existing LPV spaces in sound condition, or bathroom flooring. 5.2 Material and Installation Specifications Flooring Material: Supply and install Lux Wood Cheyenne 7.25" x 48", 20 Mil Wear Layer / 5mm Core, with 1.55mm Pad LVP (approx. 2,887 sq. ft.). Baseboard: Supply and install 4-inch Coiled Vinyl Base throughout all finished areas. Subfloor Preparation: Complete mechanical grinding and adhesive removal on existing subfloors (allowance benchmark not to exceed $2.75/sq. ft.). Subfloor must be clean, level, dry, and inspected prior to installation. Adhesive: Utilize commercial adhesive strictly complying with the flooring manufacturer�s bonding specifications and DHS facility environmental guidelines. Debris & Containment: Install temporary dust and noise containment barriers to isolate adjacent active operational spaces. Contractor is responsible for removing all scrap, old carpet, adhesive residue, and packaging off-site daily. Clearance & Inspection: Ensure all interior doors swing freely with full functional clearance over new flooring transitions. 5.3 On-Site Conditions, Security & Personnel Requirements Key Personnel: The designated Project Manager must serve as the primary technical point of contact, be available by phone/email during duty hours (0800�1600 EST), and respond to technical requests within two (2) hours. Base Security & Badging: All workers must possess valid state-issued photo IDs, wear company-identifiable attire/badges at all times, and remain escorted in Government spaces as required. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. Subject to FAR Clause 52.215-3, entitled Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes, this announcement constitutes a Request for Information for written information only. The Naval Supply System Command (NAVSUP), Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk (FLCN) is conducting market research to remain competitive in an increasingly competitive world. In accordance with Title 10 of US Code, the United States Naval Academy has a mandate to admit qualified applicants from every congressional district in the United States. INTRODUCTION The Aircraft Project Management Office (AIR PMO), under the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager Robotic Autonomous Systems (DRPM RAS), is conducting market research regarding commercially available and emerging Group 1 and Group 2 Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Training, Mission Planning, Mission Rehearsal, Simulation, and Qualification Management Systems. For market research and planning purposes, the Government is seeking information regarding industry�s ability to provide and support these capabilities at scale. Potential future demand could involve thousands of training devices, simulator stations, software licenses, or equivalent deployed units. However, no procurement quantity, acquisition strategy, or requirement has been established, and any quantities referenced in this RFI are illustrative planning assumptions only. The Government requests white papers from interested parties with commercially available or emerging capabilities. Responses will assist the Government in identifying potential solutions; understanding technical approaches, system maturity, interoperability, scalability, implementation considerations, and business models; refining capability objectives and potential requirements; and informing acquisition planning and potential procurement strategies. This RFI follows the Air PMO virtual Industry Day conducted on 03 September 2026. Participation in the Industry Day is not a prerequisite for responding to this RFI. Interested parties may respond regardless of whether they attended the event. This RFI is an independent Air PMO market research effort and is not associated with or conducted in support of the Drone Dominance Program. Simulation-based training may also reduce operational impacts associated with range availability, airspace restrictions, spectrum congestion, weather delays, aircraft maintenance requirements, and logistical constraints while supporting standardized, repeatable, and scalable training across multiple UAS platforms. title: Solicitation of a Concession Business Opportunity to Operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services within Lake Mead National Recreation Area
description: The National Park Service (NPS) has released on September 2, 2026, a business opportunity soliciting proposals to award a new ten (10) year concession contract to operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services in Lake Mead National Recreation Area. The NPS will host a site visit for entities interested in bidding on the opportunity on September 21, 2026. The site visit provides interested entities with an overview of the concession operation and a tour of the Concession Facilities (land and real property improvements assigned to the concessioner under the Draft Contract), as well as the Desert Princess vessel, which is government-owned personal property assigned to the concessioner. Site Visit Registration Registration is required to attend the site visit. To register, contact Nicole Williams, Concessions Management Specialist, Lake Mead National Recreation Area at nicole_williams@nps.gov, along with a courtesy copy to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov, no later than 12:00 pm (Pacific Time) on September 17, 2026. You must provide your name, contact information, the name of the entity interested in submitting a proposal that you represent, the primary contact for the entity, and the number and names of people in your party. Due to space constraints, the NPS limits the number of site visit attendees to a total of five (5) people per interested entity. Site visit participants are responsible for obtaining their lodging, meals, and transportation to the Concession Facilities. The operation is located at 490 Horsepower Cove, Boulder City, NV 89005. Attendance at the site visit is encouraged, but not required, to submit a proposal. The NPS will not answer questions about this prospectus or business opportunity during registration or the site visit. Interested entities must submit questions in writing after the release of the prospectus to the contact person and by the deadline that will be provided in the prospectus. Interested entities are asked not to interfere with concessioner operations during the site visit and not to film, record or photograph concessioner employees or concessioner operations. Questions Due Questions regarding the prospectus must be received, in writing, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on September 30, 2026. INTRODUCTION The Aircraft Project Management Office (AIR PMO), under the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager Robotic Autonomous Systems (DRPM RAS), is conducting market research regarding commercially available and emerging Group 1 and Group 2 Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Training, Mission Planning, Mission Rehearsal, Simulation, and Qualification Management Systems. For market research and planning purposes, the Government is seeking information regarding industry�s ability to provide and support these capabilities at scale. Potential future demand could involve thousands of training devices, simulator stations, software licenses, or equivalent deployed units. However, no procurement quantity, acquisition strategy, or requirement has been established, and any quantities referenced in this RFI are illustrative planning assumptions only. The Government requests white papers from interested parties with commercially available or emerging capabilities. Responses will assist the Government in identifying potential solutions; understanding technical approaches, system maturity, interoperability, scalability, implementation considerations, and business models; refining capability objectives and potential requirements; and informing acquisition planning and potential procurement strategies. This RFI follows the Air PMO virtual Industry Day conducted on 03 September 2026. Participation in the Industry Day is not a prerequisite for responding to this RFI. Interested parties may respond regardless of whether they attended the event. This RFI is an independent Air PMO market research effort and is not associated with or conducted in support of the Drone Dominance Program. Respondents should address the capability areas and information requested in this RFI without assuming any relationship to that program�s requirements, acquisition approach, funding, schedule, or procurement quantities. BACKGROUND Simulation-based training has the potential to enhance operator proficiency, improve training availability, increase training throughput, reduce operational risk, and provide realistic Mission Planning and Mission Rehearsal capabilities for Group 1 and Group 2 UAS. These capabilities may enable operators to safely practice in realistic and challenging operational and threat environments, emergency procedures, and degraded system behaviors that may be impractical, unsafe, or cost-prohibitive to execute using live aircraft. Simulation-based training may also reduce operational impacts associated with range availability, airspace restrictions, spectrum congestion, weather delays, aircraft maintenance requirements, and logistical constraints while supporting standardized, repeatable, and scalable training across multiple UAS platforms. The Government seeks to understand current industry capabilities, technology maturity, innovative approaches, best practices, and limitations relevant to these objectives. The Government may use information received to support capability development, requirements refinement, acquisition planning, evaluation of commercially available and emerging solutions, and potential procurement strategies. Following review of submitted white papers, the Government may invite selected respondents to participate in follow-up discussions or technical demonstrations to further assess the maturity, suitability, and applicability of proposed solutions. Selection for, or participation in, a follow-up activity does not constitute a competitive range determination, source-selection decision, commitment to procure, or preference for any future acquisition. Any invitation and associated instructions will be issued separately. The Government may elect not to conduct follow-up activities and is not obligated to provide feedback to respondents. Executive summary of the proposed solution and the operational or training problem it addresses. Description of the complete solution, including software, hardware, peripherals, hosting or deployment model, licensing, and any Government-furnished equipment or services required. title: Remote Weapon Station Industry Day
description: The Army Contracting Command -Detroit Arsenal is issuing this Special Notice (Notice ID: W912CH-27-R-A018, historically related to W15QKN26R0008 and W15QKN25X15LO) to announce an upcoming, in-person Industry Day on Wednesday, January 13, 2027 (08:30 AM - 4:30 PM EST) at the Courtyard by Marriott in Mt. Arlington, NJ. The event aims to foster market research and open collaboration regarding future RWS requirements under NAICS code 332994. Attendance is strictly limited to eligible U.S. defense contractors possessing an active Joint Certification Program (JCP) certification (DD Form 2345). All interested parties are directed to view and download the attached RWS Industry Day Notice.pdf for complete event details, security guidelines, and required registration forms. title: Beach Renourishment, Kennedy Space Center, Brevard County, Florida
description: This announcement constitutes a Source Sought Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR BIDS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The Jacksonville District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is seeking interest from prospective offerors for a potential fiscal year (FY) 2027 award of the aforementioned project. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to gauge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of various members of the Construction and Dredging Communities, to include Small Businesses, as the Government must ensure there is adequate competition amongst the potential pool of responsible contractors. The notice is also soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for this large-scale construction project exceeding $35,000,000. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to said notice or any follow-up information requested. The proposed project will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. The Jacksonville District anticipates the issuance of an Invitation For Bid (IFB). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to said sources sought notice or any follow-up information requested. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The proposed project work will consist of nourishing approximately 4.1 miles shoreline along Kennedy Space Center between FDEP Range Monuments V-366 and V-386 in Brevard County, Florida. The project includes dredging approximately 2.5 million cubic yards (MCY) of material for construction of a beach berm and dune. Beach compatible sand for the project may be dredged from up to three (3) offshore borrow areas. Chester Shoals I is located east of Cape Canaveral in State waters and is centered approximately 1.7 miles offshore of Kennedy Space Center. Kennedy Shoals and Hetzel Shoals are located east of Cape Canaveral in Federal waters and are centered approximately 4.5 miles and 10 miles, respectively, offshore of Kennedy Space Center. Project work also includes, but is not limited to, beach tilling, turbidity monitoring, environmental species monitoring, and Munitions and Explosive of Concern (MEC) support. The project will have an estimated period of performance of 280 calendar days after issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP), including 60 calendar days to commence work. Magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. The NAICS Code is 237990 Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the SMALL BUSINESS STANDARD SIZE IS $45,000,000.00. Anticipated solicitation issuance date is on or about June 1, 2027 and the anticipated bid opening day is on or about July 1, 2027. The official Synopsis citing the solicitation number will be issued on the SAM.gov Contracting Opportunities Website: www.sam.gov. title: Digital Talking Book Machines - Library of Congress
description: Amendment 2: Changes the PPQ. - - - Solicitation Amendment -0001 answers Offeror questions. Please see 030ADV27R0001 -0001, Attachment J-6, and revised Attachment J-1. - - - This public notice is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12 and utilizing FAR Part 15 procedures. The solicitation is being released as an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract competition. This contract shall include two performance areas to encompass all aspects of procuring new Digital Talking Book Machines and maintaining the new and existing stock at the Library. Performance Area 1 (PA1): DTBM DA2 Production, Parts, and Support This PA includes DA2 units, warranties, spare parts, software development, and other requirements described in Section C. NLS requires Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) version DA2 units in quantities sufficient to continue distribution to all audio readers enrolled in the program and maintain a reasonable stock to allow timely replacement of devices in the field to facilitate service, repair, or maintenance of removed devices. NLS requires support for those units including spare parts, software development, and warranty repairs. Performance Area 2 (PA2): Existing Device Support, Incumbent This PA includes proprietary spare parts and software development as described in Section C. NLS also requires repair and support services for the existing incumbent-manufactured NLS DTBM DA2 units (approximately 63,000). This includes spare parts and platform sprints to ensure the units remain safe, functional, and accessible so that the Library�s patrons have the fullest access to materials in the NLS collection. Please see all attachments for the full details of this requirement and instructions for submitting a proposal. Questions are due by 5:00pm eastern time, September 14, 2026. Proposals are due by 5:00pm eastern time, October 5, 2026.

title: Kantonsstrasse Nr. 47, Goldach/Tübach: Brücke Goldach
description:
Instandsetzung und Verstärkung der einfeldrigen Plattenbalkenbrücke zwischen Goldach und Tübach. Die Brücke wird zwischen den Stegen mittels CFK-Lamellen in Längsrichtung verstärkt, die Lager ersetzt, die Fahrbahnübergänge werden aufgehoben und beidseits werden Schleppplatten an den Widerlagern erstellt. Die beiden Staketengeländer werden ersetzt. Das Meteorwasser wird neu gefasst und über einen Mineralölabscheider in die Böschung versickert. Zur Baumassnahme gehört ein provisorischer Gerüstboden mit integriertem Fussgängersteg.


Hauptkubaturen:

  • Abbruch Beton 75 m3
  • Abbruch Belag 45 m3
  • Abbruch Abdichtung 400 m2
  • Ersatzgeländer 80 m
  • Asphalt 150 t
  • Abdichtung 400 m2
  • Beton 140 m3
  • CFK-Lamellen 190 m

title: Hindelbank ; réaménagement de la Dorfstrasse
description:
Contexte et objectifs du projet

La route cantonale n° 1 (Morat – Berne – Rothrist) est un axe routier majeur du canton de Berne. L’analyse standardisée des points faibles de ce tronçon routier a révélé la nécessité d’intervenir sur différents aspects. On constate notamment des lacunes considérables en matière de circulation cycliste et piétonne, ainsi que de respect des limitations de vitesse. Ce projet s’inscrit dans le cadre du programme d’agglomération de Burgdorf (4e génération). Les travaux doivent débuter avant le 31 décembre 2028. Un projet de construction a été élaboré en 2026. La mise à l’enquête publique du projet de construction aura lieu en novembre/décembre 2026.


L’objectif est de réaliser un projet conforme aux normes et standards en vigueur, qui tienne compte de toutes les contraintes actuelles. De plus, les objectifs du programme d’agglomération sont pris en compte dans le projet :

▪ Meilleure intégration dans le tissu urbain

▪ Amélioration de la qualité et de la sécurité pour tous les usagers de la route

▪ Élimination des points faibles


Le projet « Réfection de la Dorfstrasse » a pour objectif premier d’améliorer la sécurité routière générale.


L’objet du marché porte sur les prestations d’ingénierie relatives aux phases partielles 41 à 53, conformément au chapitre 3 du cahier des charges, ainsi qu’au tableau des prestations figurant au chapitre 2. L’ensemble des mesures de réaménagement et de rénovation à réaliser dans le périmètre du projet doivent être planifiées par le mandataire ou, si elles sont planifiées par des tiers, coordonnées et supervisées par celui-ci

title: Netherlands – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – DAS SURF Cumulus Professional Services 2023
description: De toekomst van de ICT en bijbehorende dienstverlening voor onderwijs- en onderzoek ligt volgens SURF én de leden voor een belangrijk deel in de cloud. De leden (instellingen) willen daarom flexibel gebruik kunnen maken van de cloud en deze combineren met eigen ICT-infrastructuren (hybride infrastructuur). Overgang naar de cloud is in de praktijk geen eenvoudige stap, en voor veel instellingen geldt dat er weinig ervaring mee is opgedaan. Er kunnen daardoor onverwachte uitdagingen ontstaan tijdens de uitvoering van cloud projecten alsook in de beheerfase erna. De initieel beoogde voordelen worden dan niet behaald waardoor afbreukrisico c.q. kapitaalvernietiging kan ontstaan. Om instellingen te ondersteunen bij deze uitdagingen is het dan ook gewenst om SURFcumulus Professional Services via een SURF aanbesteding voor hen beschikbaar te maken. SURF kiest ervoor om dit via een DAS te laten verlopen. De levering van SURFcumulus Professional Services is nadrukkelijk gekoppeld aan de SURFcumulus dienst. Concreet gaat het om uitvoerende, gangbare dienstverlening bedoeld voor cloud implementatie, -migratie en -beheer. Levering gebeurt op basis van vaste prijs en vaste opleverdatum. Uitvoeren/ondersteunen van cloud migraties, door middel van: Lift-and-shift migratie scenario: het zonder ingrijpende wijzigingen (deels) verplaatsen van een ICT infrastructuur uit een datacenter naar de cloud. Re-design migratie scenario: het cloud ready maken van (een deel van) een bestaande ICT infrastructuur en/of het implementeren van vervangende, nieuw te bouwen oplossingen waardoor het potentieel van de cloud optimaal benut kan worden. Leveren van cloud managed services in de (hybride) cloud infrastructuur, waaronder bijv.: Operations (accountbeheer, software update management, licentiebeheer, netwerkbeheer, backup & restore, monitoring, platformbeheer) Application management (technisch applicatiebeheer, functioneel applicatiebeheer, gegevensbeheer, applicatie configuratiebeheer) Service support (incident-, problem- & change management, multi vendor coordinatie, tweede en derdelijns support, escalatie afhandeling) Service delivery (service level management, capacity-, cost- en continuity management) Informatie beveiliging en privacy bescherming (detectie, preventie, rapportage, bijsturing). title: Maximum Length Sequence Phase Encoding for Quantum Sensor Readout
description: Quantum sensors can detect extremely small electromagnetic and magnetic signatures, which makes them powerful tools for geophysical analysis, materials detection, environmental monitoring, and scientific research. Their sensitivity also makes them vulnerable to interference from ambient RF sources, electrical noise, and outdoor or industrial environments. Traditional readout methods attempt to preserve the phase of the sensor or allow it to evolve uniformly, but these approaches can produce ambiguous results or false positives when exposed to strong interference. Los Alamos researchers developed a pseudorandom phase-encoding method that allows a quantum sensor to distinguish true target signals from substantial background noise. By applying a maximum length sequence, also called an msequence, the sensor�s phase is flipped by 180 degrees according to a designed pattern. The resulting measurement is analyzed using correlation against the known sequence, enabling accurate extraction of the intended signal even when conventional methods fail to differentiate between interference and true sensor output. Advantages Improves quantum sensor performance in noisy outdoor and industrial settings Distinguishes true sensor signals from interfering or spurious noise Reduces false positives without added shielding or multichannel detection Integrates into existing measurement protocols with minimal modification Compatible with a range of quantum sensing platforms, including magnetic and electromagnetic systems Technology Description The method embeds a defined sequence of phase inversions into the quantum sensor. Target signals track this imposed pattern because they arise from the controlled experiment, while interfering signals do not. This inherent separation allows correlation-based processing to highlight coherent responses and suppress background noise. Demonstrations using low field nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) show that both traditional CPMG-style readouts and the m-sequence-based readout detect the intended signal under ideal conditions. However, when only interference is present, the traditional readout cannot reliably separate interference from the target signal, while the m-sequence method correctly rejects the interferer. Experimental data also show strong correlation peaks for the encoded measurement and minimal correlation for AM or broadband interferers, confirming the method�s robustness in realistic outdoor and industrial noise environments. Market Applications This phase-encoded readout method supports sensing platforms in which interference can obscure weak or transient signals. Its characteristics make it relevant to a wide range of technologies, including: subsurface imaging and resource characterization in geophysical exploration quantum sensing systems deployed near infrastructure such as roads, power lines, or industrial equipment environmental and geophysical platforms that integrate seismic, muon, magnetic, or other sensing modalities detection systems that require high confidence in distinguishing real signatures from environmental noise These and related applications benefit from enhanced robustness and improved discrimination of true signals in field environments. title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Protein-Based Rare Earth Recovery via Condensation
description: Protein-Based Rare Earth Recovery via Condensation from scientists at Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a cleaner, flexible way to capture and concentrate rare earth elements from complex liquid mixtures by using a bio-inspired protein system that gathers target metals into separable clusters. The approach is designed to reduce reliance on harsher processing methods while supporting more resilient supply chains for critical materials used across energy, electronics, transportation and advanced manufacturing markets. Because the system is genetically modular, the same platform may be adapted with different Lanmodulin-type metal-binding variants to support selective capture needs across varied feedstocks. How it Works The technology modifies Lanmodulin, a protein known for strong rare earth element binding, by adding an �encapsulation peptide" to the N-terminus of the protein. Once the engineered protein binds rare earth elements in solution, the resulting protein-metal complexes can be triggered for self-assemble into biomolecular condensates, which are larger clusters that can be removed from the liquid. The material can then be separated and concentrated through various means�such as centrifugation, filtration, and sedimentation�reducing the need for immobilizing the protein on a column or other fixed support. Technical Description Rare earth elements are important to modern technologies; yet, processing and purification can be difficult and environmentally damaging. Protein-Based Rare Earth Recovery via Condensation addresses that problem through EP-LanM, an engineered version of Lanmodulin that changes its material state when rare earth elements are present. Rather than focusing only on changing which rare earth elements Lanmodulin binds, this technology changes how the protein behaves after binding, turning dissolved protein-metal complexes into recoverable droplets. The metals can be harvested from the protein droplets, and the resultant free-protein itself can be recycled into iterative separations. The protein architecture is modular, with the encapsulation peptide fused to Lanmodulin so the protein can self-assemble in response to rare earth element binding. The assembled EP-LanM-rare earth complexes can be captured through simple centrifugation, filtration, or sedimentation, which may simplify processing compared with approaches that require immobilization on a column. The modular design may also support use with other Lanmodulin derivatives that have been designed for specific rare earth affinities, creating a path toward tailored separation strategies � without requiring a full redesign of the recovery concept. Advantages Uses a bio-based protein system for rare earth element capture Concentrates rare earth elements from complex mixtures Enables separation after droplet formation Avoids the need for protein immobilization in a column-based format Supports modular adaptation with different Lanmodulin derivatives Aligns with demand for more environmentally conscious critical-material recovery methods Allows recovery and recycling of input protein Market Applications Critical Minerals Recovery (rare earth concentration, mixed metal streams) Mining and Mineral Processing (process waters, low-grade sources) Waste Recycling (recovered components, mixed recycling streams) Environmental Remediation (metal-bearing waters, industrial residuals) Biomanufacturing and Bioseparation (engineered protein recovery tools, modular capture systems) Development Status: TRL 3 U.S. Patent pending LA-UR-26-25158 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. Los Alamos researchers developed a pseudorandom phase-encoding method that allows a quantum sensor to distinguish true target signals from substantial background noise. By applying a maximum length sequence, also called an msequence, the sensor�s phase is flipped by 180 degrees according to a designed pattern. The resulting measurement is analyzed using correlation against the known sequence, enabling accurate extraction of the intended signal even when conventional methods fail to differentiate between interference and true sensor output. Advantages Improves quantum sensor performance in noisy outdoor and industrial settings Distinguishes true sensor signals from interfering or spurious noise Reduces false positives without added shielding or multichannel detection Integrates into existing measurement protocols with minimal modification Compatible with a range of quantum sensing platforms, including magnetic and electromagnetic systems Technology Description The method embeds a defined sequence of phase inversions into the quantum sensor. Target signals track this imposed pattern because they arise from the controlled experiment, while interfering signals do not. This inherent separation allows correlation-based processing to highlight coherent responses and suppress background noise. Demonstrations using low field nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) show that both traditional CPMG-style readouts and the m-sequence-based readout detect the intended signal under ideal conditions. However, when only interference is present, the traditional readout cannot reliably separate interference from the target signal, while the m-sequence method correctly rejects the interferer. Experimental data also show strong correlation peaks for the encoded measurement and minimal correlation for AM or broadband interferers, confirming the method�s robustness in realistic outdoor and industrial noise environments. Market Applications This phase-encoded readout method supports sensing platforms in which interference can obscure weak or transient signals. Its characteristics make it relevant to a wide range of technologies, including: subsurface imaging and resource characterization in geophysical exploration quantum sensing systems deployed near infrastructure such as roads, power lines, or industrial equipment environmental and geophysical platforms that integrate seismic, muon, magnetic, or other sensing modalities detection systems that require high confidence in distinguishing real signatures from environmental noise These and related applications benefit from enhanced robustness and improved discrimination of true signals in field environments. title: Accelerator-Driven Sub-Critical Molten-Salt Assembly (ADS+MSA Facility)
description: An accelerator-driven, sub-critical molten-salt nuclear system that centrally produces large quantities of tritium for fusion energy. By pairing accelerator-driven subcritical operation with molten-salt chemistry, the system offers a controllable, safety-forward pathway to produce fusion fuel, recover useful energy and convert legacy nuclear liabilities into strategic energy assets. Overview: The Accelerator-Driven Sub-Critical Molten-Salt Assembly (ADS+MSA) is a centralized nuclear facility that uses a high-power particle accelerator coupled to a liquid molten-salt system to reliably produce kilogram-scale quantities of tritium. Because the system is sub-critical, nuclear reactions only occur when driven by the accelerator, providing inherent safety and operational control. By combining proven accelerator technology with modern molten-salt chemistry, the ADS+MSA removes a major bottleneck to commercial fusion energy, recovers useful energy, and strengthens U.S. energy security and national security missions under existing Department of Energy safety frameworks rather than commercial reactor licensing. Key Advantages: Enables large-scale commercial fusion energy by providing a reliable, centralized source of tritium, eliminating the need for fusion plants to breed their own fuel and significantly reducing cost, complexity, and deployment risk. Operates in an inherently safe, sub-critical configuration in which nuclear reactions stop when the accelerator is turned off, avoiding runaway scenarios and allowing operation under DOE accelerator safety orders rather than NRC power-reactor licensing. Achieves extremely high tritium production efficiency, with tritium breeding ratios far exceeding those achievable in fusion reactor blankets, enabling kilogram-scale production with substantially lower accelerator power than earlier accelerator-only concepts. Builds on decades of proven accelerator development and growing industrial experience with molten-salt systems, reducing technical risk and enabling modular, scalable deployment as demand increases. title: Switzerland – Ironmongery work – Mittenza für Muttenz – Kulturhaus Umnutzung und Sanierung I BKP 275 Schliessanlagen
description: Die Gemeinde Muttenz plant die Sanierung und teilweise Umnutzung eines mehrgeschossigen Bestandsgebäudes innerhalb der Anlage „Mittenza“ im historischen Ortskern. Die Anlage umfasst mehrere Baukörper; Gegenstand des vorliegenden Projekts ist ausschliesslich das ehemalige Hotel- und Kongress- Gebäude. Das um 1975 erstellte Gebäude ist Teil eines Ensembles von regionaler Bedeutung und steht unter kantonalem Denkmalschutz. Nach einer Phase des teilweisen Leerstands wird das Gebäude instandgesetzt und einer neuen Nutzung zugeführt. Der grosse Saal bleibt für kulturelle und gesellschaftliche Veranstaltungen erhalten. Ergänzend entstehen Räumlichkeiten für Verwaltung, die allgemeine Musikschule sowie weitere Vereins- und Gemeinschafts- Nutzungen. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung sind die Schliessanlagen (BKP 275) für die Sanierung und Umnutzung des ehemaligen Hotel- und Kongressgebäudes. Der Auftrag umfasst die Lieferung und Montage der Schliessanlage einschliesslich der zugehörigen Komponenten sowie deren Einrichtung und Inbetriebnahme gemäss Ausschreibungsunterlagen und Leistungsverzeichnis. Dazu gehören die Abstimmung mit den beteiligten Gewerken an den Schnittstellen zu Türen und Zutrittskontrolle sowie sämtliche für die fachgerechte und funktionsfähige Ausführung erforderlichen Nebenleistungen. Das Gebäude befindet sich in einem innerörtlichen Umfeld. Während der Bauzeit ist auf die örtlichen Gegebenheiten, die Baustellenlogistik sowie auf Anwohner und angrenzende öffentliche Nutzungen besonders Rücksicht zu nehmen. Die detaillierte Beschreibung der Leistungen ist den Ausschreibungsunterlagen zu entnehmen.

title: Norway – Laundry-collection services – Hire, laundry and dry cleaning of work clothes and textiles for Dental health Rogaland.
description: Background and purpose Dental health Rogaland needs a total system for hire, collection/delivery and laundry/dry cleaning of work clothes for dental health personnel for the dental clinics in Rogaland county. The work wear shall be of a high standard, be without a logo and have good functionality and comfort. The need currently comprises 32 dental clinics and approx. 420 employees divided in 390 entire positions. The system must be able to handle changes in both manpower, number of delivery locations and seasonal variations. The aim is to ensure stable and safe access to hygienic, functional and user-ready workwear with a sufficient number of shifts per employee each day. There is also a need for a traceable and predictable textile flow between the clinics and the laundry, with easy practical handling out at each clinic and as few manual follow-up as possible. Scope The need includes hire, delivery, washing and dry cleaning of work wear for clinical use, including upper parts and trousers in white and blue. Pregnancy clothing can also be delivered for employees who need this, as well as hijab, in two different varieties. In addition there is a need for heating jackets or fleece jackets that can be used over ordinary work clothes for sedentary office work, breaks etc. There will be seasonal variations in extent. Tenderers must deliver a sufficient amount of textiles to at least one daily shift for all employees at the respective clinics. Some days there will also be a need for change of shifts during the day. The system must therefore be able to handle variations in consumption, sizes and individual needs across the clinics. Some clinics also have a need for cleaning related textiles, including mops in cotton and microfibre for floors and microfibre cloths (currently six dental clinics), mats for the entrance area to reduce dirt and water (currently ten dental clinics, approx. 20 mats), as well as health blankets/blankets (currently two clinics) for use in patient treatment when patients spend a long time in general anaesthesia. Operation and follow-up The practical textile flow is wanted organised with joint stock for all employees per clinic, with a fixed collection and delivery according to the agreed route and a system that is simple, predictable and as self-service as possible for the clinics. There is a need for hygienic and traceable handling of textiles between the clinic and the laundry. In order to provide good management and follow-up in the clinics, we would like a portal that shows stock, textile flow and an option to register changes in the clinic ́s needs. Quality and hygiene requirements The workwear and other textiles must wear high durability, tolerate frequent industrial laundry and at the same time retain the fit and colour over time. The textiles must fulfil the hygiene requirements and must be delivered in good quality and ready for use at the clinics and they must not contain health or environmentally damaging chemicals that could lead to damage to users or the environment, either during production or when used. Stable security of deliveries is another central need for this agreement.

description: Η παρούσα σύμβαση αφορά την παροχή υπηρεσιών περισυλλογής επιπλεόντων αντικειμένων και κηλίδων, καθώς και την αντιμετώπιση περιστατικών ρύπανσης από πετρέλαιο, άλλες ουσίες και φυσικοχημικά φαινόμενα (συμπεριλαμβανομένου του φυτοπλαγκτού) στον Θερμαϊκό Κόλπο. Συγκεκριμένα αφορά : Α) Την υπηρεσία καθαρισμού που καλύπτει τη γεωγραφική περιοχή από το Λιμάνι της Θεσσαλονίκης έως το Ακρωτήριο του Μεγάλου Εμβόλου (Αγία Τριάδα) στα ανατολικά, καθώς και τα Δέλτα των ποταμών Αξιού και Αλιάκμονα στα δυτικά. Β) Τη διαχείριση όλων των απορριμμάτων και κηλίδων που συλλέγονται, από το στάδιο της αρχικής συλλογής μέχρι το στάδιο της τελικής διάθεσης. Γ) Την υποβολή μηνιαίων εκθέσεων στις οποίες θα αναφέρονται οι εκτελεσθείσες κινήσεις και εργασίες ανά ημέρα, τα αποτελέσματα των εργασιών και τυχόν προβλήματα που παρουσιάστηκαν, φωτογραφικό υλικό από τις εκτελεσθείσες εργασίες και τις περιοχές εργασιών, τα είδη των συλλεχθέντων απορριμμάτων (ενδεικτικά: πλαστικό, γυαλί, μέταλλο, ξύλα, φυτικές ύλες) και έκτακτων περιστατικών ρύπανσης, τις συλλεχθείσες ποσότητες αποβλήτων ανά ημέρα εργασίας και συγκεντρωτικά ανά μήνα και τον χώρο τελικής διάθεσης αυτών. Οι παρεχόμενες υπηρεσίες κατατάσσονται στους ακόλουθους κωδικούς του Κοινού Λεξιλογίου δημοσίων συμβάσεων (CPV): 90733000-4 – «Υπηρεσίες που σχετίζονται με ρυπασμένα ύδατα». Η παρούσα σύμβαση δεν υποδιαιρείται σε τμήματα και ανατίθεται ως ενιαίο σύνολο, καθώς το φυσικό αντικείμενο είναι ενιαίο και αδιαίρετο και το έργο πρέπει να καταστεί εν το συνόλω λειτουργικό. Σε περίπτωση διαίρεσης σε τμήματα θα απαιτούνταν συντονισμός εργασιών προκειμένου να μην καταστεί η σύμβαση τεχνικά δύσκολη ή περαιτέρω δαπανηρή για την Αναθέτουσα Αρχή. Προσφορές υποβάλλονται για το σύνολο της σύμβασης. Η συνολική εκτιμώμενη αξία της σύμβασης για τη χρονική διάρκεια των δεκαοκτώ (18) μηνών ανέρχεται στο ποσό των διακοσίων εβδομήντα δύο χιλιάδων οκτακοσίων πενήντα ευρώ (272.850,00 €) μη συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% (ποσό με ΦΠΑ: 338.334,00 €). Η Αναθέτουσα Αρχή διατηρεί το Δικαίωμα Προαίρεσης για την ανάθεση πρόσθετων εργασιών τακτικού καθαρισμού και αντιμετώπισης φυτοπλαγκτού, συνολικού προϋπολογισμού έως 104.300,00 € μη συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% (ποσό με ΦΠΑ: 129.332,00 €). Ο συνολικός προϋπολογισμός της Διακήρυξης (συμπεριλαμβανομένου του Δικαιώματος Προαίρεσης) ανέρχεται στο ποσό των 377.150,00 € μη συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% (ποσό με ΦΠΑ 467.666,00 €). Η διάρκεια της σύμβασης ορίζεται σε δεκαοχτώ (18) μήνες από την υπογραφή της και ειδικότερα από την ημερομηνία ανάρτησης στο ΚΗΜΔΗΣ. Η Αναθέτουσα Αρχή διατηρεί το δικαίωμα μονομερούς άσκησης προαίρεσης, συνολικής εκτιμώμενης αξίας 104.300,00 € πλέον ΦΠΑ, υπό τους ίδιους όρους της αρχικής σύμβασης και σύμφωνα με τα αναλυτικά οριζόμενα στη Διακήρυξη, η οποία επιμερίζεται ως εξής: α) Για τους τακτικούς καθαρισμούς επιπλεόντων αντικειμένων: έως τριάντα (30) δυνητικά πρόσθετες ημέρες εργασίας (22 καθημερινές, 4 Σάββατα και 4 Κυριακές/αργίες), εκτιμώμενης αξίας 29.300,00 € πλέον ΦΠΑ. β) Για τους έκτακτους καθαρισμούς φυτοπλαγκτού: έως πέντε (5) δυνητικά πρόσθετες επιχειρήσεις καθαρισμού, εκτιμώμενης αξίας 75.000,00 € πλέον ΦΠΑ.

Z uwagi na fakt, iż opracowana przez Wykonawcę dokumentacja, będzie stanowiła opis przedmiotu zamówienia stanowiący załącznik do SWZ na realizację robót budowlanych w trybie ustawy z dnia 11 września 2019 r. Prawo zamówień publicznych Wykonawca zobowiązuje się do przygotowania dokumentacji w taki sposób, aby spełniała wszelkie wymogi ustawy Pzp. 6. Przedmiotu zamówienia nie można opisywać w sposób, który mógłby utrudniać uczciwą konkurencję, w szczególności przez wskazanie znaków towarowych, patentów lub pochodzenia, źródła lub szczególnego procesu, który charakteryzuje produkty lub usługi dostarczane przez konkretnego wykonawcę, jeżeli mogłoby to doprowadzić do uprzywilejowania lub wyeliminowania niektórych wykonawców lub produktów. W takim przypadku Wykonawca wskazuje w opisie przedmiotu zamówienia kryteria stosowane w celu oceny równoważności. Przedmiot zamówienia winien być opisany zgodnie z art. 101 Ustawy Pzp. 7. Dokumentacja techniczna winna uwzględniać zapisy art. 100 Ustawy Pzp. tj. „W przypadku zamówień przeznaczonych do użytku osób fizycznych, w tym pracowników zamawiającego, opis przedmiotu zamówienia sporządza się, z uwzględnieniem wymagań w zakresie dostępności dla osób niepełnosprawnych oraz projektowania z przeznaczeniem dla wszystkich użytkowników, chyba że nie jest to uzasadnione charakterem przedmiotu zamówienia. Ponadto należy przyjąć, że wszystkim takim odniesieniom towarzyszą wyrazy "lub równoważne". Wskazanie równoważności oferowanego rozwiązania zgodnie z art. 101 ust. 5 ustawy i na zasadach tam określonych spoczywa na Wykonawcy. 9. W przypadku opisu za pomocą norm za rozwiązania równoważne uznaje się takie rozwiązania, które zapewniają spełnienie wymagań minimalnych określonych w normie na poziomie nie gorszym niż opisano to w stosownych normach. W przypadku przywołanych w SWZ norm (jeżeli nie określono tego szczegółowo) rozumie się normy aktualne. W pozostałych przypadkach (opis przedmiotu zamówienia za pomocą ocen technicznych, specyfikacji technicznych i systemów referencji technicznych) za równoważny uważa się taki produkt, materiał czy system o parametrach technicznych, funkcjonalnych i jakościowych nie gorszych niż wymienione w opisie przedmiotu zamówienia.

Obstarávateľ určuje tieto hlavné potreby a požiadavky pre súťažný dialóg: 5.2.1. zabezpečiť zvýšenie úrovne jadrovej bezpečnosti a dlhodobú funkčnosť, spoľahlivosť, udržiavateľnosť a podporovateľnosť bezpečnostných systémov SORR, SIS a CPL, s dôrazom na plnenie bezpečnostných funkcií, ochranu do hĺbky, nezávislosť, redundanciu, kvalifikáciu a diagnostiku systémov; 5.2.2. zabezpečiť modernizáciu bezpečnostných systémov spôsobom, ktorý minimalizuje zásahy do prevádzky blokov a negatívny dopad na plánované odstávky a zároveň zabezpečí jednoznačné definovanie rozhraní modernizovaných systémov na existujúce systémy elektrárne; 5.2.3. zabezpečiť, aby navrhované technické riešenie bolo technicky, realizačne a licenčne uskutočniteľné, zohľadňovalo existujúcu projektovú, prevádzkovú a licenčnú bázu blokov EMO12 a bolo v súlade s požiadavkami Obstarávateľa, platnými právnymi predpismi, relevantnými technickými normami a požiadavkami jadrového dozoru; 5.2.4. zabezpečiť, aby navrhované riešenie bolo ekonomicky efektívne počas celého životného cyklu systémov, vrátane nákladov na projektovanie, realizáciu, licencovanie, prevádzku, údržbu, náhradné diely a riadenie zastarávania (obsolescence management); 5.2.5. zabezpečiť, aby uchádzači počas súťažného dialógu preukázali uskutočniteľnosť navrhovaného riešenia a vytvorili podklady potrebné na definovanie konečného technického, realizačného, zmluvného a obchodného riešenia predmetu zákazky a na predloženie Ponuky. 5.3. Obstarávateľ bude Zadanie (technické podklady) potrebné na prípravu a vedenie súťažného dialógu sprístupňovať postupne, s ohľadom na ich rozsah a charakter: 5.3.1. pri vyhlásení Súťažného dialógu bola sprístupnená voľne prístupná časť Zadania obsahujúca základnú Technickú špecifikáciu v rozsahu potrebnom na oboznámenie sa s predmetom SD; 5.3.2. po predložení podpísanej NDA bude sprístupnená časť Zadania obsahujúca kompletnú Technickú špecifikáciu; 5.3.3. vo fáze dialógu budú Uchádzačom postupne sprístupňované zvyšné časti Zadania, vrátane kompletných Technických požiadaviek a dostupnej projektovej, prevádzkovej a technickej dokumentácie; 5.4. Obstarávateľ bude návrhy zmluvnej dokumentácie sprístupňovať postupne, s ohľadom na jej rozsah a charakter: 5.4.1. po predložení podpísanej NDA budú sprístupnené Základné zmluvné podmienky; 5.4.2. vo fáze dialógu budú Uchádzačom sprístupnené kompletné návrhy Zmluvy o dielo a aplikovateľných zmluvných podmienok a LTSA a aplikovateľných zmluvných podmienok. Stručný opis projektu 6.1. SE ako významný výrobca elektrickej energie v Slovenskej republike pripravuje projekt Modernizácia bezpečnostných systémov SORR, SIS a CPL na blokoch EMO12. 6.2. Projekt predstavuje komplexnú modernizáciu vybraných bezpečnostných systémov jadrovej elektrárne, ktorých účelom je zabezpečenie plnenia bezpečnostných funkcií, ochrany reaktora, ochrany technologických zariadení a riadenia bezpečnostne významných funkcií v podmienkach normálnej prevádzky, abnormálnej prevádzky a projektových udalostí. 6.3. Predmetom projektu je najmä návrh, projektovanie, kvalifikácia, dodávka, montáž, skúšky, uvedenie do prevádzky a odovzdanie modernizovaných systémov SORR, SIS a CPL vrátane potrebných úprav súvisiacich zariadení, rozhraní, káblových trás, napájania, dokumentácie, skúšobných postupov, prevádzkových predpisov, výcviku a podpory počas uvádzania do prevádzky. 6.4. Projekt musí byť realizovaný tak, aby boli počas prípravy a realizácie rešpektované najmä tieto základné princípy: 6.4.1. zachovanie jadrovej bezpečnosti počas celého životného cyklu projektu a minimalizácia dopadov na bezpečnú a spoľahlivú prevádzku blokov EMO12; 6.4.2. realizácia prác v súlade s plánovanými odstávkami, prevádzkovými obmedzeniami a požiadavkami elektrárne; 6.4.3. preukázateľná kvalifikácia navrhovaných zariadení, systémov, softvéru, hardvéru a jednoznačná nadväznosť technického riešenia na existujúcu licenčnú, projektovú a prevádzkovú dokumentáciu; 6.4.4. riadenie technických, integračných, licenčných, kvalifikačných, kybernetických, realizačných a harmonogramových rizík a zabezpečenie dlhodobej servisnej podpory a technickej podpory modernizovaných systémov. 6.5. Cieľom projektu je pripraviť a realizovať také technické riešenie, ktoré bude zodpovedať bezpečnostnému významu modernizovaných systémov, bude realizovateľné v podmienkach prevádzkovanej jadrovej elektrárne, bude licenčne obhájiteľné, ekonomicky primerané a bude poskytovať dostatočnú technickú a prevádzkovú stabilitu počas ďalšej plánovanej prevádzky blokov EMO12. 6.6. Projekt si vzhľadom na svoj rozsah, bezpečnostný význam, počet rozhraní, väzbu na odstávky a licenčné požiadavky vyžaduje detailné technické prerokovanie s Uchádzačmi v rámci súťažného dialógu.

title: Tapahtumajärjestäjäpalvelut
description: Tapahtumajärjestäjäpalvelut Hankinnan kohteena on tapahtumajärjestäjäpalvelut. Puitejärjestelyyn valitaan yksi toimittaja. Hankinnan tavoitteena on hankkia laadukas ja ammattitaitoinen, ns. täyden palvelun tapahtumajärjestäjä, joka huolehtii mm. sidosryhmätilaisuuksien ja henkilöstötapahtumien järjestämisestä. Yhteistyön määrä ja sisältö vaihtelevat tapahtumittain. Tapahtumajärjestäjän vastuulla saattaa olla joko koko tapahtuman toteutus tai vain ennakkoon sovittu osa siitä. Tilaaja järjestää vuosittain noin 1–3 tilaisuutta, jossa Toimittajan palveluita mahdollisesti käytetään. Tapahtumat ovat luonteeltaan esim. seminaareja, sidosryhmätilaisuuksia ja henkilöstötilaisuuksia. Yhteen tilaisuuteen osallistuu arviolta noin 100–1 500 henkilöä. Osa tilaisuuksista järjestetään ns. hybriditilaisuuksina, joissa osa osallistujista on paikalla ja osa osallistuu verkon kautta. Valittavalta sopimuskumppaniltamme toivomme erityisesti vakuuttavia referenssejä, yhteistyökykyä, korkeaa laatutasoa, tapahtumajärjestämiseen liittyvien trendien seuraamista ja tuntemista, ideointikykyä, toimivaa alihankintaverkostoa ja hyvää englannin kielen suullista ja kirjallista taitoa. Edellytämme hyvää suomen kielen suullista ja kirjallista taitoa. Tapahtumajärjestäjältä hankittavan palvelun sisältöä on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 1 Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus.,
